newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus Airways reports H1 loss.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus Airways reports H1 loss.

text.p: Results in first half until June 30, 1996.
Pre tax loss 2.90 million profit 162 thousand
After tax loss 2.90 million profit 62 thousand
NOTES: Cyprus Airways Ltd is a government-controlled company with 20 percent of its shares floated on the Cyprus stock exchange. The group is comprised of the following companies:
The companies of the group had not prepared six monthly results for 1995 and the figures shown above are estimates calculated on the final results of the year ended December 31 1995.
A company statement said losses sustained are due to the following reasons:

- A reduction in revenue from passenger movement by three million pounds due to the reduction in the number of passengers and the lower returns from fares. This is due to a crisis in tourism and the strong competition among airlines which led to a significant drop in air fares.
- An increase in fuel costs by 0.4 million pounds.
- The negative fluctuation of foreign currencies against the Cyprus pound which resulted in a loss of 0.5 million pounds.

The results of the group include 2.6 million pounds which represents the return of fees the group paid to Eurocontrol, the air traffic control association in Europe, for flights over Cyprus between 1991 and 1995.
The money was returned through the Cyprus government.
Due to the seasonal nature of the group's activities the results of the second half will be, under normal circumstances, significantly improved compared to those of the first half.

In the results of the first six months there has been no provision for the sum of $5.2 million dollars, which Cyprus Airways is demanding from an aeroplane engine manufacturing company for an engine fault in a plane of the airline's fleet, the company said.
